report_name: California Student Data Breach at ETS Exposes Millions

threat_actors.name: Unidentified Attacker
threat_actors.description: The unidentified threat actor responsible for the data breach at Educational Testing Service (ETS) between May and September 2026. The actor used a single compromised credential to access an SFTP site and exfiltrate data belonging to millions of California students.

attack_patterns.name: Valid Accounts
attack_patterns.description: The attacker leveraged a single compromised login credential to gain unauthorized access to a secure file transfer protocol (SFTP) site managed by ETS.

attack_patterns.name: Data from Cloud Storage
attack_patterns.description: The threat actor performed data exfiltration by accessing and copying files containing student PII from the SFTP server, which functioned as a cloud-based data repository for the state.

attack_patterns.name: Automated Exfiltration
attack_patterns.description: The exfiltration of massive datasets over a prolonged period of four months suggests a potential for automated data collection and transfer from the compromised SFTP site.

identities.name: Educational Testing Service (ETS)
identities.description: A key contractor for the California Department of Education whose SFTP site was compromised, leading to the exposure of student data.

identities.name: California Department of Education (CDE)
identities.description: The government agency responsible for California's public school system. The data of students under its purview was exposed in the breach at its contractor, ETS.

identities.name: California Public School Students
identities.description: A class representing the millions of current and former California public school students whose personal information was exposed in the breach.

infrastructure.name: ETS SFTP Site
infrastructure.description: A secure file transfer protocol (SFTP) site managed by ETS that was compromised using a stolen credential, allowing the attacker to exfiltrate millions of student records.

indicators.name: Anomalous Large Data Egress from SFTP Server
indicators.pattern:
title: Anomalous Large Data Egress from SFTP Server
id: 2b9a1c3d-e4f5-4a8b-9c1d-ef0123456789
status: experimental
description: Detects network connections using SFTP/FTP protocols which should be monitored for unusually large data transfers that deviate from baseline activity, as seen in the ETS data breach.
references:
  - https://www.latimes.com/california/story/2026-10-16/state-testing-student-data-hack
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-10-18
tags:
  - attack.t1530
  - attack.exfiltration
level: medium
logsource:
  category: network_connection
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    DestinationPort:
      - 21
      - 22
    Initiated: 'true'
  condition: selection
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate large file transfers.
indicators.description: Detects outbound SFTP/FTP connections which should be monitored for unusual volume, a pattern observed in the ETS data breach where large volumes of student data were exfiltrated over four months.

indicators.name: Unusual SFTP Server Login
indicators.pattern:
title: Unusual SFTP Server Login
id: 8d7c6b5a-4f3e-4d2c-b1a0-987654321fed
status: experimental
description: Detects SFTP server authentications, which should be correlated with source IP, geolocation, and time to identify activity indicative of credential compromise.
references:
  - https://www.latimes.com/california/story/2026-10-16/state-testing-student-data-hack
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-10-18
tags:
  - attack.t1078
  - attack.initial_access
level: medium
logsource:
  product: linux
  service: sshd
detection:
  selection:
    keywords:
      - 'subsystem request for sftp'
  condition: selection
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate remote logins by authorized users.
indicators.description: Detects SFTP server logins. Such events should be audited for unusual IP addresses, geolocations, or times, which could indicate a compromised credential as used in the ETS breach.

indicators.name: Interactive Login by Service Account
indicators.pattern:
title: Interactive Login by Service Account
id: f1e0d9c8-7b6a-4987-8654-3210fedcba98
status: experimental
description: Detects interactive logins by accounts typically used for automated services. This could indicate account misuse or compromise.
references:
  - https://www.latimes.com/california/story/2026-10-16/state-testing-student-data-hack
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-10-18
tags:
  - attack.t1078
  - attack.defense_evasion
level: high
logsource:
  product: windows
  service: security
detection:
  selection:
    EventID: 4624
    LogonType: 2
    TargetUserName|endswith:
      - '$'
    TargetUserName|contains:
      - 'svc_'
      - 'srv_'
  condition: selection
falsepositives:
  - Administrators performing interactive maintenance using a service account.
indicators.description: Detects interactive logins from service accounts, which is anomalous behavior and could indicate that an account intended for automated processes has been compromised.
